title: Payments (Stripe)
summary: subscriptions sold on the web through Stripe Checkout: the entitlement is computed once on the server and rides on the session, a guard and a route layout read it, the checkout return is settled from Stripe's own Checkout Session, every webhook is recorded and deduplicated, `provider` says who sold a row so only that seller may manage it, and with no `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` billing is inert rather than broken
postScaffold: yarn db:generate && yarn db:migrate --name subscription  (the two tables: `subscription`, which @better-auth/stripe owns, and `webhook_event`, the deduplicated trail)
billing is OFF until STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is set: no client, no plugin, no checkout — `yarn dev`, `yarn dev:mock` and every gate run that way on purpose
to turn it on, set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, STRIPE_PRICE_MONTHLY and STRIPE_PRICE_ANNUAL in .env (the boot fails naming whichever is missing); STRIPE_PORTAL_CONFIGURATION is optional

webhooks in development: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/auth/stripe/webhook` — its `whsec_…` is STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and that path is in KIT_RAW_BODY_PATHS so the bytes Stripe signed reach the handler unparsed
mock mode boots with no subscription: the paywall is what a guarded route sends you to, and the mocked checkout settles into an active plan
